requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of IPv4 ICMP redirects on node1.
requirements.summary: The final sysctl file sets accept_redirects to 0 for all, default, eth0, and lo. Every live scope was 0 before restart and remained 0 after a boot-ID-changing restart, directly demonstrating persistence.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of IPv4 source-routed packets on node1.
requirements.summary: The final sysctl file sets accept_source_route to 0 for all, default, eth0, and lo. Every live scope was 0 before restart and remained 0 after the verified restart.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes are satisfied. The final live kernel values and persisted configuration were directly verified, followed by a complete node-restart protocol: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, independently confirmed boot-ID change, and recovered services, writable storage, network devices, configuration hash, and hardened values.
limitations: Package-health collection timed out in both lifecycle snapshots, so package consistency could not be independently compared; the executor timeline contains no package-changing command.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The initial configuration creation, wildcard compatibility attempt, sysctl-service applications, explicit-interface correction, and reboot all had clear task or mandatory restart-evidence roles. The ineffective wildcard state was superseded by the final explicit configuration and did not remain. Post-executor observations show no failed services, no new socket exposure, and only ordinary reboot-generated temporary-file changes.
